360 Political Ecology (360PE) welcomes evidence-based feedback, editorial enquiries, correction requests, research collaboration proposals, and responsible media enquiries.

## Enquiries

- **Research and interdisciplinary collaboration** — scholarship, joint research initiatives and shared evidence projects
- **Editorial correspondence** — article submissions, publication proposals and contributions related to the [ten areas of analysis](topics.qmd)
- **Evidence and corrections** — source questions, data issues, factual clarifications and substantive corrections
- **Media and educational enquiries** — interviews, explanatory materials and educational partnerships

## Publication Corrections and Evidence Requests

360PE is committed to transparency, accuracy and responsible research communication.

When requesting a correction or clarification, please include, where possible:

- The title of the article or publication
- The relevant section, page or paragraph
- The specific claim, data point or interpretation requiring clarification
- A reliable supporting source or explanation of the concern

Substantive corrections will be evaluated against the platform's [Editorial Standards](editorial-standards.qmd).

## Editorial Independence

360 Political Ecology is an independently operated, research-informed platform. Its editorial decisions are not directed by the founder's academic affiliations.

For more information about the publication and its leadership, visit [About 360PE](about.qmd) and [Founder and Editorial Leadership](founder.qmd).
